seoTitle: Free Hash Generator for MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256
metaDescription: Generate MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 hashes of any text at once. Free, uses UTF-8 and runs in your browser without uploading your text.
intro: Type or paste text and get its MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 hashes at the same time, as lowercase or uppercase hex.
why:
A hash is a short fingerprint of data. You use it to check that a downloaded file or a copied string was not altered, to build cache keys, to compare a value against a published checksum, or to reproduce a hash that an API expects.

This tool computes five common algorithms in one go, so you do not run five commands. MD5 and SHA-1 are included because many old systems still publish them, but they are broken for security uses; prefer SHA-256 or better. Text is hashed as UTF-8. The calculation runs in your browser, so the text you hash is never uploaded. Hashing is not encryption and cannot be reversed.
howTo: Type or paste the text to hash into the box.
Read the five hashes shown, one per line, each labelled with its algorithm.
Tick "Uppercase hex" if the system you compare against uses capital letters.

faq.a: Use SHA-256 or SHA-512 for integrity checks. MD5 and SHA-1 have known collision attacks, so avoid them where an attacker could craft input. They remain fine for catching accidental corruption or matching old checksums.

faq.q: Can I use this to store passwords?
faq.a: No. Fast hashes like these are the wrong tool for passwords because they can be guessed billions of times per second. Use a slow password hash such as bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2, which are available on this site.

faq.q: Why does my hash differ from another tool?
faq.a: The usual causes are a trailing newline or space, different line endings, or another text encoding. This tool hashes the exact UTF-8 bytes of what you typed, so even one extra character changes everything.
